primitives.verbatim_quote: First, we evaluate each player's offense and defense in the SPM framework based on three basic categories of skills: scoring, rebounding, and ball-handling.

primitives.breakdown_regime: When player skill ratings are constant or when lineup composition remains static.

primitives.name: Synergy Calculation Method
primitives.verbatim_quote: The results of the simulations measure the effectiveness of individual players as well as the 5-player lineup, so we can then calculate the synergies of each NBA team by comparing their 5-player lineup's effectiveness to the "sum-ofthe-parts." We find that these synergies can be large and meaningful.
primitives.assumptions: Individual player contributions are linearly additive; synergy emerges from non-linear interaction terms.
primitives.breakdown_regime: When individual player ratings approach zero or when lineup composition is fixed.

layer2.mapping: Synergy calculation mirrors vector space projection onto subspace spanned by effective lineups.
layer2.telemetry: Deviation of observed from predicted team performance metrics.

primitives.verbatim_quote: Indeed, our framework is able to generate mutually beneficial trades between teams.

reasoning_traces.think:
The Skills Plus Minus (SPM) framework operates by assigning discrete skill ratings to players across core categories—scoring, rebounding, and ball-handling. These ratings are used to simulate game outcomes, which allows for quantifying how much a lineup performs beyond the sum of its parts. The synergy calculation method compares actual team performance against a baseline derived from individual player ratings, capturing emergent properties of team chemistry. This enables the detection of mutually beneficial trades by identifying scenarios where swapping players improves both teams’ synergy scores. The framework avoids traditional ranking systems that fail to account for context-dependent value, instead modeling value as a function of roster composition. It leverages probabilistic simulation to compute expected outcomes under varying lineups, thereby enabling ex-ante trade optimization. The mathematical structure supports iterative refinement through feedback loops involving empirical performance data and updated skill estimates.
